<Rep. Donald S. Beyer, Jr.>: I am proud to co-lead this simple bill with Mr. Smucker, the Claiming Age Clarity Act.
This has been endorsed by AARP.
This bill remedies terminology confusion to help communicate plainly to beneficiaries the differences in Social Security Benefits at different claiming ages. When workers across the country are claiming benefits early, they might not be aware that doing so reduces their monthly benefit amount.
This allows beneficiaries to understand the advantages and disadvantages to them of claiming social security benefits at different ages.
For example: Under the current structure and jargon, it is not apparent to beneficiaries that a worker that claims Social Security at age 62, with a monthly benefit of $1,400, could have instead earned $1,500 per month by delaying their claiming by just one year, or $1,600 by waiting two.
Those who are able to postpone claiming their benefits are almost always better off when they do, it not only increases the expected payout over their lifetime, but also provides better protection against outliving one's savings!
Not all workers are able to postpone claiming, but this bill will help de-mystify the process of claiming or postponing claiming these hard-earned benefits.
Currently the terminology is as follows:
• Early Eligibility Age, Full Retirement Age,
and Delayed Retirement Age
Under this bill, the terminology would become more straightforward and become:
• Minimum benefit age, standard benefit age,
and maximum benefit age
This is a simple, yet in my opinion helpful update; It is a small fix that will affect some beneficiaries, but it will provide some clarity and transparency for those that are able to postpone claiming. This might also help alleviate customer service backlogs that many of our constituents deal with by removing confusion where possible.
While this doesn't solve the big picture on social security which this committee presides over, nor does it fix the data privacy, customer service, or staffing disaster DOGE and this Administration has put on this agency. But it will help on the margins and I am glad that this little bill is seeing the light today.
And I am proud of my work with Congressman Smucker on this and I thank him for this partnership.
I urge my colleagues to vote yes on this bill!
Don Beyer.
